catalog_citation: von Prince, Kilu. 2023. Word units in the Oceanic predicate complex. Project description (15 pp.), kiluvonprince.de, restating von Prince 2015 (A Grammar of Daakaka, Mouton Grammar Library 67, De Gruyter Mouton, ch. 2 §2.4 Prosody, pp. 34-37). Corroborated second-hand by Hopperdietzel, Jens Philipp. 2020. Resultatives: A view from Oceanic verb serialization. PhD diss., Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, §4.3.2.1 'Prosody in Daakaka', p. 136 (citing von Prince 2015: 34ff).
catalog_locator: von Prince 2023: p. 4 (PDF p. 4 of 15), §1 'Starting point', paragraph on vowel harmony and word stress; Hopperdietzel 2020: printed p. 136 = PDF p. 154, §4.3.2.1.
catalog_quote: I have argued in von Prince (2015) that Daakaka has no word stress, which suggests all the more that vowel harmony is central to marking word boundaries. [von Prince 2023: 4] ... Regarding its prosodic features, it is significant to note that Daakaka lacks lexical stress according to the parameters of duration, (fundamental) frequency and intensity (von Prince 2015: 34ff). Yet, Daakaka exhibits boundary tones that correspond to the syntactic unit of a clause (TP or CP). In utterance-medial position these boundary tones are characterized by a pitch rise, while in utterance-final position pitch contour lowers (or stays the same). ... The pitch rises are always on the final syllable of the intonational phrase (IP). Therefore, high IP boundary tones indicate match with clausal boundaries which gives rise to a hat shaped intonation contour of a simple clause (von Prince 2015: 35). [Hopperdietzel 2020: 136]

new_statements.rule_in_words: According to von Prince's grammar as reported by Hopperdietzel, Daakaka has no lexical (word-level) stress: duration, F0 and intensity do not single out a syllable within the word. Prominence is phrasal: a high boundary tone on the final syllable of each non-final intonational phrase (clause) and a low/level boundary at utterance end, giving a hat contour.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the word (no lexical stress) and the phrase/clause (boundary tones on the IP-final syllable); based on a phonetic analysis of connected speech, not citation forms. Second-hand: Hopperdietzel summarises von Prince 2015 §2.4 (pp. 34-37); the primary pages were not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Daakaka proper (Baiap/Sesivi area, west-southwest Ambrym) = daka1243; Hopperdietzel 2020 and von Prince's work are on the same variety. Lynch & Crowley 2001 suspect Tryon's separate 'Port Vato' communalect (port1240?) may be a dialect of the same language; von Prince's grammar is the description of record for daka1243 only.
